channel.title: The Ottawa Citizen - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Ottawa Citizen (ottawacitizen.com)

item.title: Hum: Where's the pho? Co Oi Kitchen offers refreshingly different Vietnamese fare
item.description: The cosy eatery in the Glebe opened last fall and specializes in Northern Vietnamese dishes.

item.title: Sounding the alarm over internet safety: Ottawa youths take case to Parliament
item.description: The federal government has said it would consider re-tabling Bill C-63, known as the Online Harms Act, sometime this year.

item.title: Baby in stroller left with minor injuries after near-miss with driver in Kanata
item.description: A stroller reportedly tipped over following a near-miss with a car in Kanata on Thursday morning, leaving a baby with minor injuries.

item.title: OCDSB supervisor says he cancelled speaker who would cost as much as an EA's salary
item.description: Ottawa's largest school board is also no longer paying for advertising designed to attract students for other boards, says Bob Plamondon.

item.title: Public servants ordered back to office four days per week as of July
item.description: Executives will be required back in the office full-time as of May.

item.title: Ottawa Senators goalie Linus Ullmark a late scratch with illness
item.description: James Reimer was to start in net against the Philadelphia Flyers, while Hunter Shepard was recalled from Belleville to serve as backup.

item.title: City of Ottawa asked to consider winter parking ban on bus-crowded Grove Avenue
item.description: The parking ban is one move being considered to accommodate transit buses on the narrow Old Ottawa South roadway.

item.title: Union president says 'a strike vote on remote work' could be coming
item.description: Public service unions responded with anger after the federal government announced it's sending public servants back to the office for four days a week.

item.title: Senators centre Tim Stutzle scores in OT to secure victory in Philadelphia
item.description: With 74 seconds left in the third period, Jamie Drysdale of the Flyers broke Senators goaltender James Reimer's bid for a shutout -- but the Senators won in overtime.

item.title: Senators player grades: Stutzle scores OT winner, Reimer near perfect in win over Flyers
item.description: Tim Stutzle had a whale of a shift to close out the game in overtime, Nick Cousins found a scoring touch and James Reimer was near perfect for the Ottawa Senators in a 2-1 victory against the Philadelphia Flyers.
